notes_for_editor: Thin evidence, same pattern as Spooner. The only source is the tnlandforms list: coordinates, elevation (no unit labelled) and the codes BLL-64692 and gfc-125. The record's elevation_m of 30.5 matches 100 ft, so the story reads the figure as feet and says so. The same page says GFC provided coordinates for 118 towers (BLL-nnn) and an older GFC list covers 203 towers (gfc-nnn); the story gives the codes as the list writes them. Searches found no fire tower history for Springfield or Effingham County. A search snippet (towerdex.com/tower/1255815, not fetched) describes a 299.9 ft antenna structure in Springfield registered to the Effingham County Board of Commissioners. It is probably a communications structure and is not treated as this lookout; a human could check whether it sits on the same site. The story is about 100 words, under the 120-word guide floor, on purpose. The NHLR and FFLOS counts come from the local crawl copy; its full NHLR list has no Springfield. Fact-check 2026-10-21: removed the US that had been added to the BLL and GFC codes (the list reads BLL-64692 and gfc-125), replaced the unlabelled feet figure with a stated reading, added the missing footnote to the first sentence, and narrowed 'No source describes' to the sources read. The Tom Dunigan credit is not on the Georgia page; it comes from the same site's Tennessee page footer.
